Hinge Health, Inc. (NYSE: HNGE). US virtual-care provider. Sells a
musculoskeletal (MSK) care program — app + wearable motion sensor (Enso) +
remote physical therapists and health coaches — to employers and health plans,
billed per ENGAGED covered life. Expanding into migraine (launched), GI

Selected: **D. Product-Platform Hybrid**, in transition toward **B. Quality
Compounder**. Weighted Blended Engine.

Reason 1 — Installed-base monetization is the actual mechanism. Revenue =
(clients) x (eligible covered lives) x (yield) x (price). The company discloses
2,929 clients [Actual] and a yield of 4.45% [Actual, FY2026 company guidance].
This is textbook installed-base monetization, which is archetype D's defining

its MONETIZATION LOGIC, not for any hardware content. Hardware is estimated at
well under 1% of revenue; capex is $1M/yr on $588M revenue [Actual].

Reason 2 — It has already graduated out of Option-Led (E). The framework's
E->D transition test is Core Revenue >50%, GM >30%, FCF+ for 2 consecutive
quarters. HNGE clears all three by a wide margin: 100% of revenue is core,
GAAP gross margin 86% [Actual, Q2'26], and FCF was positive in FY2024 ($48M),
FY2025 ($171M) and TTM ($290M) [Actual, pack]. It is not a narrative company.

Reason 3 — It has NOT yet earned Quality Compounder (B). B requires ROIC > WACC
for 3 consecutive years and established installed-base monetization. Installed-
base monetization: YES. Three years of ROIC > WACC: **NO** — FY2023 and FY2024
GAAP operating income were negative (-$131M, -$32M) [Actual, pack]. HNGE has
roughly two quarters of positive GAAP operating income.

Transition-scoring: 1 of 3 D->B criteria met = 33%. Below the 50% threshold for
a mandated Blended Engine on transition grounds; however I blend anyway for a
different and more important reason (0-3).

0-3. STEP 0-2 — VALUATION ENGINE SELECTION
Selected: **Blended Engine 3 (Product-Platform Hybrid) as the structural frame,
implemented as Engine 1 (traditional DCF) core + Engine 4 (expectation-driven)
option overlay.**

Weights: Engine 1 core DCF 85% | Engine 4 option layer 15%.

* Engine 1 alone would value HNGE as a mature compounder and assign ZERO to the

  That understates the asset.
* Engine 4 alone would value a company with $858M guided revenue and a guided

* Engine 1 + Engine 4 overlay is precisely the Engine 3 "Core Anchor + Platform
  Premium" construction, with the platform premium capped and probability-
  weighted rather than assumed. That is what I have built.

Why NOT Engine 2: Revenue is contractual and recurring, priced per engaged life,
not by a commodity price. Cycle-normalized mid-cycle EPS would destroy the one
signal that matters (yield and client growth).
Why NOT Engine 5: There is no single binary approval gate. FDA 510(k) clearances
are incremental, not existential.

Engine 3 "Core Anchor Stack": I did NOT use the prescribed 0.4 EV/Sales + 0.4

deviation from the letter of Engine 3, retained in spirit.

Conviction penalty applied for transition period: -0.5 step (Layer 5).

Engine 2 (Cyclical) would have "normalized" revenue to a mid-cycle level and
thrown away a doubling of the client base. Engine 4 alone would have produced a
$100+ valuation on narrative alone. Engine 1 alone would have produced a fair
value too low to be honest about the contracted GI revenue.
